comparisons.peer_topic: SBLC Credit Quality and Consumer Breakdown
comparisons.peer_summary: At December 31, 2024, the notional amounts of SBLCs classified as investment grade and non-investment grade were $25.0 billion and $10.1 billion, while consumer SBLCs amounted to $1.0 billion.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and BAC disclose the classification of specific financial instruments into investment grade and non-investment grade categories. C reports that 56% of its 'Classifiably managed loans' were investment grade as of Dec 31, 2024, evaluated via internal risk classifications. BAC reports specific notional amounts for Standby Letters of Credit (SBLCs), with $25.0 billion classified as investment grade and $10.1 billion as non-investment grade, also based on the credit quality of the underlying reference name. While C provides a percentage of a total pool and BAC provides absolute dollar amounts, both disclosures address the breakdown of credit quality within specific asset classes (managed loans vs. SBLCs) using investment grade/non-investment grade taxonomies.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, approximately 56% and 74% of these loans, respectively, were rated investment grade.

(2) The notional amounts of SBLCs and financial guarantees classified as investment grade and non-investment grade based on the credit quality of the underlying reference name within the instrument were $25.0 billion and $10.1 billion at December 31, 2024, and $23.6 billion and $9.7 billion at December 31, 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: The firm assigns regulatory risk ratings to loans based on U.S. federal bank regulatory agency definitions, with 93% of total loans rated pass/non-criticized as of December 2024 and 92% as of December 2023.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and GS disclose credit quality metrics for their loan portfolios using internal or regulatory risk ratings. C states that 56% of its managed loans were rated investment grade as of Dec 31, 2024, based on internal risk classification. GS states that 93% of its total loans were rated 'pass/non-criticized' as of December 2024, based on definitions provided by U.S. federal bank regulatory agencies. Both disclosures quantify the proportion of high-quality (investment/pass) loans within their respective loan books, though they use different rating terminology ('investment grade' vs 'pass/non-criticized') and basis (internal vs. regulatory definitions).

Total loans included 93% of loans as of December 2024 and 92% of loans as of December 2023 that were rated pass/non-criticized.

comparisons.peer_topic: HTM securities credit quality and ratings
comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, all Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities were rated investment grade, current, and accruing, with approximately 99% rated at least AA+ based on external or internal risk ratings.
comparisons.comparison: Both C and JPM disclose the credit quality composition of their financial assets, highlighting a majority investment-grade status. C reports that 56% of its Classifiably managed loans were investment grade. JPM reports that 100% of its Held-to-Maturity (HTM) securities were rated investment grade. While both entities report high credit quality, the asset classes differ (managed loans vs. securities) and the metrics differ in specificity (56% investment grade vs. 100% investment grade with 99% rated AA+ or better). Both rely on risk ratings to assess credit quality.

sentences.text: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, approximately 56% and 74% of these loans, respectively, were rated investment grade.

At both December 31, 2024 and 2023, all HTM securities were rated investment grade and were current and accruing, with approximately 99% rated at least AA+ (based upon external ratings where available, and where not available, based primarily upon internal risk ratings).

comparisons.peer_summary: 98% of the HTM securities portfolio consisted of investment grade U.S. agency, Treasury, and Agency CMBS securities with an assumption of zero credit losses, while non-investment grade holdings primarily included Non-agency CMBS with insignificant expected credit losses.
